claim.pdf_says: 13.4.5.2 General formats, Format 3 (report): the CODE-SET clause is printed as [ CODE-SET { IS alphabet-name-1 [ alphabet-name-2] / { | FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1 | / | FOR NATIONAL IS alphabet-name-2 | } } ] -- i.e. the INNER brace around the two FOR phrases carries a pair of vertical CHOICE INDICATOR bars just inside it (a full-height bar immediately after the inner '{' and another immediately before the inner '}'). Verified by 300 dpi crop of the region; underlined words on the two rows are ALPHANUMERIC and NATIONAL.
claim.markdown_says: [ CODE-SET { IS alphabet-name-1 [ alphabet-name-2] / { FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1 / FOR NATIONAL IS alphabet-name-2 } } ]
claim.why_it_matters: Per 5.2.6.4, a pair of vertical bars just inside a brace means one or more of the enclosed alternatives may be specified, each at most once, in any order. Without the bars a brace means EXACTLY ONE. The markdown therefore makes 'CODE-SET FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alpha-1 FOR NATIONAL IS alpha-2' -- a legal Format 3 FD entry that specifies both phrases -- look illegal, and also forbids the reversed order. This is the same construct that page 372 (Format 1) transcribes CORRECTLY with bars ('{ | FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1 | }'), so the two formats of the same clause now disagree in the markdown.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by independent pixel-level inspection of the 300 dpi render; the claim is accurate as written and no rejection criterion applies.

(1) WHAT THE PRINTED GLYPHS ARE. Rendered E:/Temp/specrecon/v373/spec_p373.png (2550x3300 @ 300dpi) and cropped the CODE-SET region (page box 330,1790-1720,2170) at 2x and 6x. Scanning ink-column groups across the horizontal band covering the two FOR rows (page y 1940-2125) yields this left-to-right sequence of glyphs, with widths that discriminate curvy brace glyphs (~19 px) from thin vertical rules (2 px): outer '{' at x=616-634 (w19) | inner '{' at x=665-683 (w19) | VERTICAL RULE at x=696-697 (w2) | 'FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1' / 'FOR NATIONAL IS alphabet-name-2' text | VERTICAL RULE at x=1554-1555 (w2) | inner '}' at x=1568-1586 (w19) | outer '}' at x=1613-1631 (w19) | outer ']' stem at x=1641-1642 (w2). A separate tall-vertical-stroke scan gives the two rules IDENTICAL vertical extents, y=1952..2109 (run length 157-158 px each), spanning exactly the two FOR rows -- a matched pair. For scale, the outer bracket stems are at x=371-372 and x=1641-1642, both y=1826..2145 (320 px), spanning all three rows.

So I see, with my own eyes and confirmed by measurement, two thin full-height vertical bars whose horizontal positions place them UNAMBIGUOUSLY as the innermost enclosure: the left bar is to the RIGHT of the inner '{', and the right bar is to the LEFT of the inner '}'. They are choice indicators just inside the inner brace, not something enclosing the inner brace, and not stray rule art. They are not the outer bracket stems (different x, different height), and they are not letter strokes (2 px wide, 157 px tall, isolated with whitespace on both sides).

(2) THE BARS ARE GENUINELY ABSENT FROM THE MARKDOWN. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 16023 is the complete Format 3 CODE-SET transcription: '[ CODE-SET { IS alphabet-name-1 [ alphabet-name-2] / { FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1 / FOR NATIONAL IS alphabet-name-2 } } ]'. I inspected the surrounding lines 16011-16033 (the whole Format 3 block through the meta-language term table): there is no '|' bar anywhere, on that line or any adjacent line, and page 373 carries NO figure note at all. So this is not text that was merely reflowed, wrapped, or moved to a neighbouring line -- the tokens do not exist in the transcription.

(3) NOT FURNITURE OR FORMATTING. Choice indicators are normative meta-language, not typography. 5.2.6.4 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md offset 164017) reads: 'Choice indicators are a pair of bars, |, that enclose a portion of a general format. When enclosed by braces, one or more of the alternatives contained within the choice indicators shall be specified, but any single alternative shall be specified only once. ... The alternatives may be specified in any order.' Dropping the pair silently reclassifies the inner brace from one-or-more-in-any-order to exactly-one, which is a change in the set of legal source programs -- precisely the meaning change the claim asserts.

(4) THE CROSS-REFERENCE CHECKS OUT. Page 372's Format 1 (sequential) at lines 15981-15983 DOES transcribe the identical construct with the bars intact -- '{ | FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1 | }' / '{ | FOR NATIONAL IS alphabet-name-2 | }' -- and its figure note at line 15987 explicitly warns that per 5.2.6.4 'a CODE-SET may carry the FOR ALPHANUMERIC phrase alone, the FOR NATIONAL phrase alone, or both, in either order.' So the markdown now contradicts ITSELF about the same clause across two formats of one subclause, which independently corroborates that page 373 is the defective side and page 372 is the correct one.

(5) MINOR CLAIM DETAILS ALSO VERIFIED. In the 6x crop, CODE-SET, ALPHANUMERIC and NATIONAL are underlined; FOR and IS are not -- matching the claim's underline statement.

I attempted to refute on every listed ground and could not. Verdict: genuine normative content loss, accurately described.
verdict.corrected_description: The claim is accurate as written; no correction to its substance is needed. Two refinements for the fix-up work. (a) Precise printed nesting, measured from the 300 dpi render: '[' CODE-SET '{' <row1: IS alphabet-name-1 [ alphabet-name-2]> / '{' '|' <FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1 / FOR NATIONAL IS alphabet-name-2> '|' '}' '}' ']'. The bar pair (2 px rules at page x=696-697 and x=1554-1555, both y=1952..2109) is the INNERMOST enclosure, sitting just inside the inner brace pair (19 px curvy glyphs at x=665-683 and x=1568-1586), which in turn sits inside the outer brace pair (x=616-634 and x=1613-1631) inside the outer bracket (stems x=371-372 and x=1641-1642, y=1826..2145). Only the inner brace of the second alternative is bar-enclosed; the outer brace choosing between the 'IS alphabet-name-1' alternative and the FOR-phrase group is a plain exactly-one brace, and the outer CODE-SET bracket is a plain optional bracket. (b) Two additional, non-normative defects on the same page that should be repaired in the same edit, since the whole Format 3 figure has to be re-transcribed anyway: page 373 renders Formats 2 and 3 as flattened one-line plain text with '/' alternation instead of the fenced box-drawing figure style used for Format 1 on page 372, and it carries no figure note recording the underlined required words or the choice-indicator semantics (page 372 has both). The fix should re-transcribe Format 3 as a fenced figure with the bars restored and add a figure note mirroring line 15987's, so the two formats of 13.4.5.2 agree.
